name: log_append_smoke
purpose: TASKS 214: the proof that a run's log keeps everything written to it. probes/log_append_smoke.sh writes one line from the Windows shell, 2,000 from a WSL child under probes/wsl_capped.sh and /usr/bin/time - the arrangement both damaged runs of 14 November had - and three more from the shell. When the run has ended, `python probes/log_append_check.py probes/results_m1/log_append_smoke.log --lines 2000` says whether the log is whole; the check is a second command and not part of the job, because the job's own writer is still draining the pipe while the job runs. Run this after any change to how tools/runspec.py launches a job, and before trusting a log that two processes wrote

estimate.basis: measured 14 Nov 2026: about three seconds, of which the WSL child's 2,000 lines are most

memory.basis: the child runs under a 1,024 MB cgroup cap and prints; nothing is computed
